chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan both narrated to me from al-Hasan ibn Mattil, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibrahim ibn Uqbah, from al-Hasan al-Khazzaz al-Washsha, from Abi al-Faraj, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when he passed through the area behind Kufah. He stopped there and prayed two Rak'ah. Then he moved forward a little and prayed another two Rak'ah. Then he moved forward a little further and prayed another two Rak'ah. Then he said, 'This is the location of the grave of the Commander of the Believers.' I said, 'May I sacrifice myself for you! What were the other two locations on which you prayed?' He replied, 'The location of the head of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and the location of the pulpit of the Qa'im (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.مِنْبَرُ الْقَائِمِ: The pulpit of the Qa'im (Imam al-Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: Where are the graves of Imam Ali, Imam al-Husayn, and the pulpit of the Mahdi located according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the spatial sanctity of Kufah by linking the resting place of Imam Ali with the martyrdom site of Imam al-Husayn and the future throne of the Mahdi, illustrating the continuity of divine authority. The Imam’s ritual of praying two Rak'ah at each spot serves as a practical validation of these locations, reinforcing their status as key pilgrimage sites in Shia jurisprudence and theology.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 5. My father and Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan both narrated to me from Ḥasan ibn Mattīl, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Ibrāhīm ibn ‘Uqbah, from Ḥasan Al-Khazzāz Al-Washā, from Abil Faraj, from Abān ibn Taghlib, who said:

I was with Abī ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) when he passed through (the area) behind Kūfah. He stopped there and prayed two Rak’ah. Then he moved forward a little and prayed another two Rak’ah. Then he moved forward a little further and prayed another two Rak’ah. Then he said, “This is the location of the grave of the Commander of the Believers (a.s.).” “May I sacrifice myself for you! What were the other two locations on which you prayed?” I asked. “The location of the head of Ḥusain (a.s.) and the location of the pulpit of the Qā`im (a.s.),” Imam (a.s.) replied.
